thread:
Incident Bot: INCIDENT ALERT: cont-batch path p99 spike detected in us-west-2 (streaming path)

Maria H: saw the alert — p95 ~220ms but p99 jumping to ~3.2s across multiple hosts. :eyes:

Samir: confirmed on dashboards. Spike started ~4629998800, correlates with a clusterwide increase in mixed-seqlen requests. p99 is across both hosted and dedicated pools.

David L: are we seeing streaming stalls (stalling on kv fetch) or packing delays (waiting for batch fill)?

Maria H: quick look — logs show a lot of long-seqlen requests blocking packer for several seconds. Also observe continuous-batcher queue growth and a few 'kv cache thrash' logs.

Jess (eng-oncall): adding traces — one example request id 0x7a3f; timeline shows waiting in packer for 1.8s then scheduling into a huge batch, then backend decode fine. Streaming frames show backpressure.

Samir: initial mitigation idea: reduce max_batch_size and reduce batch wait timeout for cont-batch pools to avoid huge batches forming behind long sequences. Also consider enabling per-seqlen fairness if available.

Maria H: agree. Rolling a config change now to limit max_batch_size to 8 for cont-batch in us-west-2 and set min_batch_wait_ms to 3ms (from 12ms).

Ops Bot: deploy started for service=cont-batcher region=us-west-2 by user=maria; change-id=chg-4629-01

David L: while that's deploying, can we temporarily route streaming-sensitive traffic to streaming-only path (no cont-batch) for impacted customers? We have routing policy 'streaming-fallback' that can be toggled per-customer.

Samir: yep. I'll flip fallback for top-5 high-volume customers showing errors. Will post list in a sec.

Samir: flipping routing for customers: alpha-app, beta-search, gamma-embedters, delta-chat, epsilon-prod — done. Confirmed small drop in errors for those flows.

Maria H: cont-batcher config patch rolled, packer logs show immediate drop in giant batch formation. p99 trending down from 3.2s -> around 1.1s in telemetry.

David L: good. But we still see p99 ~1.1s system-wide. What's left? KV eviction churn still high on a subset of nodes.

Jess (eng-oncall): looks like certain sessions with long sequence lengths maintain large KV caches and are being unfairly prioritized by scheduler. There's a scheduler weight bug where seqlen weight was inverted for mixedlen workloads.

SRE Pager: that weight inversion was in the 2.4.1 runtime patch we rolled last month. Could be reintroduced by recent autoscale events. Suggest a temporary per-node scheduler override: disable seqlen weighting and use FIFO with max-batch=6.

Samir: applying per-node override to 3 nodes showing the worst churn: node-a12, node-a13, node-a19. Command:

```bash
# apply scheduler override
ssh root@node-a12 "systemctl set-environment SCHED_POLICY=fifo && curl -XPOST http://localhost:8080/admin/override -d '{\"max_batch\":6}'"
```

Ops Bot: override applied to node-a12,a13,a19 by user=samir; change-id=chg-4629-02

Maria H: post-override, those nodes' kv hit-rate stabilized, packer queue latency dropped ~70% for that cohort. Global p99 now ~520ms — still above SLO but much better.

David L: we should open a short incident runbook entry and notify Product and CS for potential customer impact; some queries hit degraded latency earlier.

Jess (eng-oncall): I'll draft a quick customer-impact note: indicate elevated tail latency for streaming during 4629998800-4629999400 window, mitigated by batching config & routing. No data loss, but perceived slow responses for heavy-long requests. ETA for permanent fix: next-week scheduler patch + more aggressive per-seqlen packing.

Samir: action items captured:
- root cause: mixed-seqlen heavy workload + scheduler weight inversion -> large batch formation + KV thrash
- short-term mitigations: reduce max_batch, reduce batch_wait, per-node scheduler overrides, routing fallback for top customers
- next steps: revert the weight inversion in 2.4.2, add automatic per-seqlen backpressure + packer fairness, add alert to detect growing mixed-seq queue depth

Maria H: tagging @sre on the rollback plan. Any objections rolling a 2.4.2 candidate to staging with weight fix today? We can smoke test replay with synthetic mixedlen load.

SRE Pager: +1. We'll run the canary on staging and then a limited production canary (2 nodes) during low-traffic window.

David L: assign owners: Samir to own prod mitigations config changes, Maria to lead postmortem + customer note, Jess to own follow-up alerting and eval prompt sets to catch regressions.

Jess (eng-oncall): noted. I'll add regression evals: new mixedlen promptset with 30/70 short/long distribution; baseline p95/p99 target <200ms/<600ms respectively.

Ops Bot: p99 metric for cont-batch us-west-2 updated: before=3.2s; after mitigations=~0.52s; routing-only customers improved to ~0.2s.

Maria H: handoff: I'm oncall until 0700. Samir will remain reachable for config rollbacks. If p99 creeps back above 700ms, escalate to SRE pager immediately and enable full streaming-route fallback.

David L: thanks all. I'll start the post-incident ticket and link traces/logs + the commands used in the run.

Incident Bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied, monitoring for recurrence. severity=medium; initial classification: performance (tail latency) due to scheduling fairness + mixed sequence lengths.

Jess (eng-oncall): final note — we need longer-term changes: smarter packer that splits very-long sequences into separate micro-batches preventing head-of-line blocking, and better KV cache size accounting per-session.

Maria H: agreed. moving to postmortem. :white_check_mark:
